# `streaming_user_daily_watch_time_possible`

> Nobody watches more than 24 hours in a day — shared or bot accounts, or duplicated events.

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain | [streaming](README.md) |
| Layer | **gold** — evaluated by the `gold` gate |
| Model | `gld_streaming__daily_user_activity` (`streaming_gold_staging.gld_streaming__daily_user_activity`) |
| Column | `watch_seconds` |
| Check | `value_between` |
| Severity | `error` — a violation **stops the pipeline** |
| Defined in | [dbt/models/streaming/gold/_gold.yml](../../../dbt/models/streaming/gold/_gold.yml) |

## What it checks

`watch_seconds` is between 0 and 86400 (inclusive).

## When it fails

The `gold` task of `medallion_streaming` fails, `publish_gold` doesn't run, and the batch is never added to `streaming_gold`: consumers keep the batches published before. `quality_report` marks the run as blocked and sends the alert, if one is configured.

The rows that broke the rule in its latest evaluation are kept in `dq_audit.streaming_user_daily_watch_time_possible`.

## Tested by

Scenario **`impossible_watch_time`**: one user watches 40 full movies in a day: rows valid, day impossible.

```bash
make generate DOMAIN=streaming SCENARIO=impossible_watch_time BATCH=2026-10-20_impossible_watch_time
make pipeline DOMAIN=streaming BATCH=2026-10-20_impossible_watch_time
```
